questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Which of the following ecological pyramids can be inverted?
A. Pyramid of energy
B. Pyramid of number
C. Pyramid of biomass
questions.solution:
The pyramid of energy is always upright because the flow of energy is unidirectional from producer to consumer level. The energy content is maximum in producers. The energy decreases at each trophic level of the food chain, as part of the energy is lost as heat, and the major part of the energy is liberated during respiration for use in various activities.
Only 10 % of the energy of the previous trophic level is received by the next trophic level, as proposed by 10 percent law of Lindeman (1942). 

Pyramid of biomass is a graphical representation of biomass present per unit area at different trophic levels. Tree and grassland ecosystems are upright as total biomass of plants (producers) in a specific area is more than that of herbivores (primary consumers) and it gradually decreases at each successive trophic level. It is least in top carnivores.

Marine biomass pyramid is often inverted as the producers are very small and have limited mass.

Pyramid of numbers is a graphical representation of a number of individuals presents per unit area at different trophic levels. 
In, most ecosystems, the number of producers is maximum. Producers thus can support fewer herbivores and herbivores can support still fewer carnivores and so on. Thus the number of top carnivores is too small to support any other trophic level and does not act as prey to any other organism.
In the parasitic food chain, at each successive trophic level, the number of the organisms is higher than in the preceding one, and the size decreases gradually at a successive level. Thus, the shape of the pyramid may be inverted.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Identify the correct sequence of steps involved in the process of decomposition.

(a) Humification

(b) Catabolism

(c) Fragmentation of detritus

(d) Leaching

(e) Mineralization
questions.solution:
Decomposition is a process in which the physical and chemical breakdown of complex organic matter will take place with the help of decomposers. The basic steps involve-

Fragmentation of detritus – Leaching – Catabolism – Humification – Mineralization.

A)  Fragmentation of Detritus: Small invertebrate animals called detritivores or detritophages feed on detritus, e.g., earthworms, termites they bring about its fragmentation.
B) Leaching: Part of water-soluble substances present in the fragmented and decomposition detritus (e.g., sugars, inorganic nutrients) go down into the soil horizon by percolating water and get precipitated as unavailable salts.

C) Catabolism: It is carried out by saprotrophic bacteria and fungi. They secrete digestive enzymes over the fragmented detritus. The enzymes degrade complex organic compounds into simple inorganic substances.
D) Humification. It is the process of decomposition of detritus to form humus. Humus is a dark-coloured, amorphous, more or less decomposed organic matter rich in cellulose, lignin, tannins, resin, etc. and is highly resistant against microbial action. It undergoes decomposition at an extremely slow rate. Humus is slightly acidic, colloidal, and functions as a reservoir of nutrients.

E) Mineralization. It is the release of inorganic substances by saprophytic microbes (e.g.. CO2, H2O, minerals) from organic matter or humus during the process of decomposition. They are formed along with simple and soluble organic substances when digestive enzymes are poured over organic matter by saprotrophic microbes.

Ecosystem characteristics that change during succession:

ii) Little diversity to a high degree of diversity i.e., increase in the number of species.

v) Aquatic or dry conditions to mesic conditions i.e, both Hydrarch and Xerarch succession lead to medium water conditions (mesic), neither too dry (xeric) nor too wet (hydric).
vi) Vegetational changes, in turn, affect food and shelter for various types of animals. Thus, as succession proceeds, the number and types of animals and decomposers also change.

questions.solution: An ecosystem is a functional unit of nature, where living organisms interact among themselves and also with the surrounding physical environment. Ecosystem varies greatly in size from a small pond to a large forest or a sea. Forest, grassland and desert are some examples of terrestrial ecosystems; pond, lake, wetland, river and estuary are some examples of aquatic ecosystems. Crop fields and an aquarium may also be considered as man-made ecosystems or artificial ecosystems. These are the ecosystems that are maintained by the man with certain manipulation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Based on a 10% law of energy transfer, identify values for A, B, and C in the figure given below.
questions.solution: The 10% law was proposed by Lindemann in 1942. The transfer of energy from one trophic level to another trophic level is accompanied by loss of energy at each level or step. When the plants are eaten by the herbivore, approximately 10% of energy in the food is fixed into animal flesh, whereas 90% is consumed in ingestion, respiration, maintenance of body heat and other activities. Similarly, when a carnivore consumes that herbivore, again approimately 10% of energy is fixed. Therefore, at each transfer, only 10% of the total energy is actually available to the next trophic level. It is called 10% law.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the below given statements with respect to three important steps of decomposition: fragmentation, leaching and catabolism. Select the correct option.
(i) Detritivores {e.g., earthworm) breakdown detritus into smaller particles.
(ii) Water soluble inorganic nutrients go down into soil horizon and get precipitated as unavailable salts.
(iii) Decomposers (e.g., bacteria and fungi) secrete digestive enzymes and degrade detritus into simpler inorganic substance.
  Leaching Fragmentation Catabolism
(a) (i) (ii) (iii)
(b) (iii) (ii) (i)
(c) (ii) (i) (iii)
(d) (ii) (iii) (i)
questions.solution: The process of decomposition can be categorised as fragmentation of detritus, leaching and catabolism. Fragmentation of detritus is the process that causes breakdown of detritus into smaller particles. It is primarily due to the action of detritus feeding invertebrates (detritivores, e.g., termites, earthworms, etc.). The detritus gets pulverised when passing through the digestive tracts of animals. Due to fragmentation, the surface area of detritus particles is greatly increased. The extracellular enzymes released by bacteria arid fungi carry out catabolism, i.e., enzymatic conversion of the decomposing detritus to simpler and inorganic substances. Leaching is the process by which dissolved nutrients are moved into lower layers of soil or groundwater to form unavailable salts.

questions.subject: Botany

questions.solution: In most ecosystems, all the pyramids, of number, of energy and biomass are upright, i.e., producers are more in number and biomass than the herbivores, and herbivores are more in number and biomass than the carnivores. Addionally, energy at a lower trophic level is always more than that at a higher level.

questions.solution: Each trophic level has a certain mass of living material at a particular time called the standing crop. The standing crop is measured as the mass of living organisms (biomass) or the number in a unit area. When the lower levels have lower standing crop than the higher level, the pyramid will be inverted, as in the case of the pyramid of biomass in an aquatic ecosystem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is Gross primary productivity (GPP)?
options: It refers to the environmental factors.
Number of plants in an ecosystem.
It is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis.
Solar energy exposed to plants in an ecosystem.
questions.solution:
Primary productivity is of two types:

A. Gross primary productivity (GPP): It is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis.

B. Net primary productivity (NPP): It is the biomass available for the consumption of heterotrophs (herbivores and decomposers).

A part of GPP is utilized by plants in respiration (R), whereas the remaining is available for the next trophic level. Hence, NPP = GPP - R

questions.q: The available biomass for the consumption to herbivores and decomposers in an ecosystem is
questions.solution: Gross primary productivity of an ecosystem is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis. A considerable amount of GPP is utilised by plants in respiration. Gross primary productivity minus respiration losses (R), is the net primary productivity (NPP). It is the available biomass for the consumption to heterotrophs (herbivores and decomposers)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is correct about the humus?
options: Black colored organic and inorganic material
Dark brown colored crystalline organic and inroganic material
Black colored crystalline organic and inorganic material
Dark brown colored amorphous organic material
questions.solution: Humus is a dark, organic material that forms in soil when plant and animal matter decays. The amorphous material helps it retain water and nutrients.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In case of plant succession, when climax is reached, the net productivity of the ecosystem
questions.solution: In the early stages of plant succession, photosynthesis is more than respiration (P > R). In the climax stage, huge respiration of living biomass occurs and photosynthesis is equal to respiration (P / R = 1 or P = R). Hence, net productivity becomes stable, when the climax stage is reached in plant succession.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: If decomposers are removed, what will happen to the ecosystem?
options: Rate of decomposition of mineral increases
questions.solution: The ecosystem will be filled by plant and animal wastes as there will be no decompositon of waste and the minerals will not get solubilized in the soil for the mineral cycle.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Secondary carnivores occupy the
options: First trophic level of a food chain
Second trophic level of a food chain
Third trophic level of a food chain
Fourth trophic level of a food chain
questions.solution: Producers are the first trophic levels, primary consumers or herbivores are at the second trophic level, secondary consumers or primary carnivores are at the third trophic level, whereas the tertiary consumers or secondary carnivores or scavengers are at the fourth trophic level.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following animals may occupy more than one trophic level in the same ecosystem at the same time?
questions.solution: Sparrow is a primary consumer when it eats seeds, fruits, etc. and a secondary consumer when it eats insects and worms.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of these Eltonian pyramids are correctly described?
options: Pyramid of numbers- may be erect or inverted, Pyramid of biomass- may be erect or inverted, Pyramid of energy- may be erect or inverted
Pyramid of numbers- always erect, Pyramid of biomass- may be erect or inverted, Pyramid of energy- may be erect or inverted
Pyramid of numbers- may be erect or inverted, Pyramid of biomass- always erect, Pyramid of energy- may be erect or inverted
Pyramid of numbers- may be erect or inverted, Pyramid of biomass- may be erect or inverted, Pyramid of energy- always erect
questions.solution: Energy keeps on decreasing in successive trophic levels. Hence, producers will have maximum energy while top carnivore will have the least energy. Hence, the pyramid of energy is always erect and never inverted. Pyramids of numbers and biomass may be upright or inverted.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In the forest ecosystem, yeasts, molds, and mushrooms are grouped as
questions.solution: The decomposers are those living organisms that decompose the dead body of producers, consumers and are known as reducers or transformers or osmotrophs. These are heterotrophic organisms that break up the dead bodies of plants and their waste products. They include fungi like yeasts, molds, and mushrooms and certain bacteria like Bacillus subtilis and Pseudomonas fluorescens etc. The enzymes secreted by these organisms digest the dead organisms and the debris into smaller bits or molecules. These molecules are absorbed by the reducers. After taking energy, the reducers release molecules to the environment as a chemical to be used again by the producers.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Based on the diagram given below, choose the correct statement from the following.
options: It is a pyramid of energy depicting the ocean ecosystem.
It is a pyramid of biomass which shows a small standing crop of phytoplankton supporting a larger standing crop of zooplankton.
It is a pyramid of biomass of a grassland ecosystem with standing crop of primary consumers supporting that of primary producers.
It shows the pyramid of number of the plankton population in an ocean ecosystem.
questions.solution: Each trophic level has a certain mass of living material at a particular time called the standing crop. The standing crop is measured as the mass of living organisms (biomass) or the number in a unit area. An ocean ecosystem is largely dominated by the plankton population. The given diagram shows an inverted pyramid of biomass with a small standing crop of phytoplankton supporting a large standing crop of zooplankton.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is/are considered as limitations of the ecological pyramids?
options: It does not take into account the same species belonging to two or more trophic levels
It assumes a simple food chain.
Saprophytes are not given any place in ecological pyramids despite playing an important role in the ecosystem.
questions.solution: There are certain limitations of ecological pyramids such as it does not take into account the same species belonging to two or more trophic levels. It assumes a simple food chain, something that almost never exists in nature; it does not accommodate a food web. Moreover, saprophytes are not given any place in ecological pyramids even though they play a vital role in the ecosystem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Plant succession occurring in a water body is called:
questions.solution: A hydrosere is a plant succession which occurs in an area of fresh water such as in oxbow lakes and kettle lakes. In time, an area of open freshwater will naturally dry out, ultimately becoming woodland. During this change, a range of different landtypes such as swamp and marsh will succeed each other.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is the correct set of events involved in the process of decomposition?
questions.solution: Detritivores (e.g., earthworm) break down detritus into smaller particles. This process is called fragmentation. By the process of leaching, water-soluble inorganic nutrients go down into the soil horizon and get precipitated as unavailable salts. Bacterial and fungal enzymes degrade detritus into simpler inorganic substances. This process is called catabolism. It is important to note that all the above steps in decomposition operate simultaneously on the detritus. Humification and mineralisation occur during decomposition in the soil.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: This flowchart is a simplified model of Phosphorous cycle. Identify labeling A and B.
questions.solution: This is a terrestrial ecosystem as it begins with rocks. Phosphorus is present in rocs as phosphates. When they weather, a small amount of phosphates dissolve in soil and reach the plants. They are absorbed by the roots of the plants. Animals will feed on plants and obtain phosphorus. When plants and animals die they are decomposed by bacteria releasing phosphorus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the incorrect statement.
options: Energy always decreases with increases in trophic level.
Secondary succession is faster than primary succession.
Ecological pyramids cannot explain all the vital functions of any ecosystem.
The amount of nutrients present in the soil at any given time is referred to as the standing crop.
questions.solution:
The amount of nutrients, such as carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, calcium, present in the soil at any given time is referred to as the standing state.

Each trophic level has a certain mass of living material at a particular time called the standing crop. The standing crop is measured as the mass of living organisms (biomass) or the number in a unit area.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following sequences is correct in a hydrarch succession?
options: Zooplankton, free-floating plants, reed swamp, scrub, forest
Phytoplankton, rooted submerged plants, free-floating plants, marsh meadow, scrub, forest
Phytoplankton, free-floating plants, marsh meadow, reed swamp, scrub, forest
Phytoplankton, free-floating plants, rooted submerged plants, reed swamp, scrub, forest
questions.solution:
Both hydrarch and xerarch successions lead to medium water conditions (mesic): neither too dry (xeric) nor too wet (hydric).
In primary succession in water, the pioneers are the small phytoplanktons, they are replaced with time by rooted-submerged plants, rooted-floating angiosperms followed by free-floating plants, then reed swamp, marsh-meadow, scrub and finally the trees. The climax again would be a forest. With time the water body is converted into land.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The pyramid of numbers in a pond ecosystem is
questions.solution: In a pond ecosystem, phytoplanktons are producers which are maximum in number, though their biomass is less as compared to consumers. Thus, the pyramid of number is always upright for any aquatic ecosystem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The diagram/flow chart represents which of the sedimentary biogeochemical cycle?
questions.solution:
Biogeochemical cycles are of two types:
(a) Gaseous: Biogenetic materials involved in circulation are gases eg. N2,O2,CO2 etc.
(b) Sedimentary: Biogenetic materials involved in circulation are non-gaseous eg. P2, Ca, S, etc forms rocks.

The flow chart represents the phosphorus biogeochemical cycle occurring in a terrestrial ecosystem. The phosphorus cycle is a sedimentary cycle and its reservoir pool is lithosphere.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Proportion of reproductive age group is higher than pre-reproductive groups in
options: More than one option is correct
questions.solution: The reproductive age group includes members between 15–45 years of age in humans. In the triangular age pyramid, the pre-reproductive age group is more than the reproductive age group, while in the bell-shaped pyramid, pre-reproductive age group is equal to that of the reproductive age group.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is the correct sequence in the food chain?
options: Fallen leaves →<math></math> bacteria → insect larvae →  birds
questions.solution: This is because phytoplankton is eaten by zooplankton which in turn is eaten by fishes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Pheretima and its close relatives derive nourishment from :
options: decaying fallen leaves and soil organic matter
small pieces of fresh fallen leaves of maize, etc.,
questions.solution: Earthworm derives its nutrition from decaying fallen leaves and soil organic matter. Thus, the type of feeding in earthworm is detritus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Which of these is/are limitation/s of ecological pyramids?

I. Decomposers are not given any place in ecological pyramids.
II. Ecological pyramids do not accommodate a food web.
III. Ecological pyramids may be upright or inverted.
IV. They don't consider omnivores in two different trophic levels.
questions.solution: Ecological pyramid is a graphical representation of relationships between organisms at different trophic levels. The base of the pyramid represents producers, whereas the apex represents tertiary consumers. Ecological pyramid considers one organism at one trophic level and does not consider omnivores. It assumes that nature has a simple food chain, but actually there are complicated interconnected food chains called food webs. Decomposers which help in recycling the energy are also not given any place.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of these are common to hydrach succession and xerarch succession?
questions.solution: Hydrarch succession begins in water bodies and continues till mesic conditions are obtained. Xerarch succession begins in dry land and continues till mesic conditions are obtained. Mesic condition in both successions is the same, neither too dry nor too wet. The community here is in near equilibrium with the environment and is called the climax community. It is a forest.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Identify the likely organisms (1), (2), (3) and (4) in the food web shown below.
questions.solution: Food web is a network of food chains or feeding relationships by which energy, and nutrients are passed on from one species of living organisms to another.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Most animals in deep oceanic water are
questions.solution: The animals like crustaceans, polychaetes, and microorganisms that are living in deep oceanic waters are called benthos and are also called as scavengers or detrivores.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: An inverted pyramid of _____________ may be observed in ____________ communities.
questions.solution: The pyramid of energy is always upright for all communities as producers always have higher energy. For aquatic communities number of phytoplanktons are more in number but their biomass is less as compared to consumers, thus pyramid of biomass is inverted for aquatic communities.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The proportion of assimilated energy consumed in respiration is highest in
questions.solution: The proportion of assimilated energy consumed in respiration in producers is 20%, in herbivores: 30% and in carnivores: 60%. As the trophic level increases, the energy spent on respiration increases.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The main role of bacteria in the carbon cycle involves
options: digestion or breakdown of organic compounds
questions.solution: Bacteria are essential decomposers in nature. They play a vital role in the recycling of nutrients by causing the breakdown of dead organic matter; thus, they play a critical role in the carbon cycle. The most important bacterium involved in the carbon cycle is Pseudomonas denitrificans.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:

(i)  Primary succession is a very slow process taking thousands of years for the climax to be reached.
(ii)  The energy at a higher trophic level is always more than at a lower level.
(iii)  Bacterial and fungal enzymes degrade detritus into simpler inorganic substances. This process is called fragmentation.
(iv)  All succession, whether taking place in water or on land, proceeds to a similar climax community: the mesic condition.

Which of the two above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Pyramid of energy is always upright and can never be inverted because when energy flows from a particular trophic level to the next trophic level, some energy is always lost as heat at each step. Addionally, energy at a lower trophic level is always more than at a higher level.

Detritivores (e.g., earthworm) break down detritus into smaller particles. This process is called fragmentation. Bacterial and fungal enzymes degrade detritus into simpler inorganic substances. This process is called catabolism.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The process of degradation of humus and release of inorganic nutrients by microbes is called
questions.solution: Humus is a dark coloured substance, resistant to microbial action. When it degrades, inorganic nutrients are released. This is called mineralization.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following uses maximum energy?
questions.solution: Primary producers are the autotrophs that produce energy, carbohydrates, through photosynthesis by capturing solar energy. Producers occupy the first trophic level having the greatest biomass or gross primary production (GPP). When energy gets transduced from producers to herbivores and to carnivores, only 10% of energy is transferred from one trophic level to another trophic level. Hence, producers receive the maximum energy.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Photosynthetic efficiency is represented by XIncident total solar radiation.

The 'X' in this equation represents
questions.solution:
The efficiency of photosynthesis is the amount of biomass a plant can produce in a given amount of light. The amount of biomass produced by producers in an ecosystem is gross primary productivity.
Photosynthetic efficiency = Gross primary productivity / Incident total solar radiation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Based on the simplified cycle given below, choose the option with the accurate labellings for A, B, C and D.
questions.solution: The natural reservoir of phosphorus is rock, which contains phosphorus in the form of phosphates. When rocks are weathered, minute amounts of these phosphates dissolve in soil solution and are absorbed by the roots of the plants. Herbivores and other animals obtain this element from plants. The waste products and the dead organisms are decomposed by phosphate-solubilising bacteria releasing phosphorus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Find out the correct statement:
options: Trophic level represents a functional level, not a species as such.
A given species never occupies more than one trophic level in the same ecosystem at the same time.
In most of the ecosystems, producers are less in number and biomass than the herbivores.
Pyramid of energy can never be upright.
questions.solution: A given species can occupy more than one tropic level in the same ecosystem at the same time, but a given species cannot occupy more than one tropic level in the same food chain. In most ecosystems, producers are maximum in number and biomass than herbivores. Pyramid of energy is always upright.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In a terrestrial ecosystems such as forests, maximum energy is found in
questions.solution: <math><mtext></mtext></math> T<sub>1 </sub>or first tropic level in a terrestrial ecosystem is occupied by producers, which trap solar energy and transfer it to successive tropic level. Maximum energy is always present in T<sub>1</sub> .

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
In how many of the following, primary succession will occur?
(Abandoned farmland, newly created pond, bare rock, burnt forest)
options: Newly created ponds, bare rock, bandoned farmlands and burnt forests
Newly created ponds and bare rock
Abandoned farmlands, bare rocks and burnt forests
questions.solution: When succession occurs in an area where no living organism ever existed; it is called primary succession and when it takes place in areas that have lost all living organisms that had existed there; it is called secondary succession. Newly created ponds, bare rock are examples of primary succession. Abandoned farmlands and burnt forests are examples of secondary succession.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Identify the correct number of food chains in the given food web.
questions.solution: In an ecosystem, the various food chains are interconnected with each other to form a network called a food web. The interlocking of many food chains is called a food web. Simple food chains are very rare in nature. This is because each organism may obtain food from more than one tropic level. In other words, one organism forms food for more than one organism of the higher trophic level.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A fowl consumes grains. What will we call the rate at which new organic matter is produced by this fowl?
questions.solution: The amount of biomass or organic matter produced by plants by photosynthesis per unit area and over a period of time is called primary productivity. It is divided into gross and net primary productivity. The rate of production of organic matter by plants through photosynthesis is called gross primary productivity and the net primary productivity is the availability of biomass for consumption by heterotrophs. The rate at which the new organic matter is produced by consumers is called secondary productivity. Here fowl or chicken is a consumer.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is expected to have the highest value (gm /m<sup>2</sup>/yr) in an ecosystem?
questions.solution: Gross productivity is the total quantity of biomass produced by plants per unit area per unit time. GPP is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The sequence of communities of primary succession in water is
options: Phytoplankton, sedges, free-floating hydrophytes, rooted hydrophytes, grasses and trees.
Phytoplankton, free-floating hydrophytes, rooted hydrophytes; sedges, grasses and trees.
Free-floating hydrophytes, sedges, phytoplankton, rooted hydrophytes, grasses and trees.
Phytoplankton, rooted submerged hydrophytes, floating hydrophytes, reed swamp, marsh meadow and trees.
questions.solution: In the primary succession in water, the pioneers are small phytoplanktons. They are replaced with time by rooted submerged plants, then by floating hydrophytes, sedges grasses and finally trees.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In an aquatic ecosystem, ______________ is the major conduit for energy flow.
questions.solution: In an aquatic ecosystem, GFC is the major conduit for energy flow. As against this, in a terrestrial ecosystem, a much larger fraction of energy flows through the detritus food chain than through the GFC. Detritus food chain may be connected with the grazing food chain at some levels: some of the organisms of DFC are prey to the GFC animals, and in a natural ecosystem, some animals like cockroaches, crows, etc., are omnivores. This natural interconnection of food chains makes it a food web.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Find the incorrect statement.
options: In a terrestrial ecosystem, a larger fraction of energy flow occurs through detritus food chain.
In the aquatic ecosystem, a major conduit for energy flow is grazing food chain.
Detritus food chain is not at all connected with grazing food chain at any level.
Natural interconnection of food chain makes it a food web.
questions.solution: In nature, the detritus food chain is connected with grazing food chains at some levels; some of the organisms of DFC are preys to the GFC animals, and in the natural ecosystem, some animals like cockroaches, crows, etc., are omnivores.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is correct for secondary succession?
options: It begins on a bare rock
It occurs on a deforested site
It is similar to primary succession except that it has a relatively fast pace
questions.solution: Secondary succession is one of the two types of ecological succession of a plants life. As opposed to the first, primary succession, secondary succession is a process started by an event (e.g. forest fire, harvesting, hurricane, etc.) that reduces an already established ecosystem (e.g. a forest or a wheat field) to a smaller population of species, and as such secondary succession occurs on preexisting soil whereas primary succession usually occurs in a place lacking soil.

The total amount or number of living things or of one kind of living thing (such as an uncut farm crop, the fish in a pond, or organisms in an ecosystem) in a particular area at any given time is called standing crop.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Osmotrophs are components of
options: both grazing and detritus food chains
neither grazing nor detritus food chain
questions.solution: Microbes that release enzymes on dead organisms, break them into simpler organic compounds and the absorb them are called osmotrophs or micorconsumers or decomposers. Examples are bacteria and fungi; they are components of the detritus food chain.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: By the process of leaching, _________ nutrients go down into the soil horizon and get precipitated.
questions.solution: Leaching is a process involved in decomposition. In this inorganic nutrients which are soluble in the water go down into the soil horizon and get precipitated as unavailable salts.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not a functional aspect of ecosystem?
questions.solution: Stratification in the field of ecology refers to the vertical layering of a habitat, the arrangement of vegetation in layers. It classifies the layers (singular: stratum, plural: strata) of vegetation largely according to the different heights to which their plants grow. Species diversity is defined as the number of different species present in an ecosystem and relative abundance of each of those species. Diversity is the greatest when all the species present are equally abundant in the area. Thus, both are the structural aspects of the ecosystem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: According to Robert Constanza, what percentage of the total cost of various ecosystem services is used for nutrient recycling and recreation activity?
options:
Nutrient recycling Recreation
Less than 10% More than 10%

Nutrient recycling Recreation
Less than 10% Less than 10%

Nutrient recycling Recreation
More than 10% More than 10%
questions.solution:
Robert Constanza and his colleagues have very recently tried to put price tags on nature’s life-support services. Researchers have put an average price tag of USD 33 trillion a year on these fundamental ecosystem services, which are largely taken for granted because they are free. This is near twice the value of the global gross national product GNP which is USD 18 trillion.

Out of the total cost of various ecosystem services, the soil formation accounts for about 50%, and contributions of other services like recreation and nutrient cycling, are less than 10% each. The cost of climate regulation and habitat for wildlife is about 6% each.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The secondary productivity means
options: Rate of increase in the biomass of autotrophs
Rate of increase in biomass of heterotrophs
The rate at which the organic molecules are formed in an autotrophs.
The rate at which the organic molecules are used in an autotrophs
questions.solution: Secondary productivity is the rate at which organic matter or biomass is stored at the level of consumers.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements. With respect to the ecological pyramid, mark the correct statements.

a. In most of the ecosystems, pyramids of number, energy and biomass are upright.
b. Producers are generally more in number or biomass than herbivores in an upright pyramid.
c. Herbivores are less in number and biomass than carnivores in an inverted pyramid.
d. Energy content is higher at a lower trophic level than that at a higher trophic level.
options: a, b, and c are correct
a, b and d are correct
questions.solution: All the statements explain the characteristics of pyramids. In most ecosystems, all the pyramids of number, energy or biomass are upright, i.e., producers are more in number and biomass than the herbivores, and herbivores are more in number and biomass than the carnivores. Also, energy at a lower trophic level is always more than that at a higher level.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In hydrarch succession, the stage which comes immediately after submerged free-floating plant stage is
questions.solution: The successive seral stages of hydrarch succession are phytoplankton stage, submerged plant stage, submerged free-floating plant stage, reed-swamp stage, marsh-meadow stage, scrub stage, and finally, forest stage.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following statements about ecological succession is incorrect?
options: A community that is in near equilibrium with the environment and that is called a climax community.
The gradual and fairly predictable change in the species composition of a given area is called ecological succession.
Primary succession takes place in those areas which somehow lost all the living organisms that existed there.
At any time during primary or secondary succession, natural or human induced disturbances (fire, deforestation, etc.), can convert a particular seral stage of succession to an earlier stage.
questions.solution: When one species occupy an area leading to declining or disappearance of other species; this changes in the composition of species in any given area is called ecological succession. When succession occurs in an area where no living organism ever existed; it is called Primary Succession and when it takes place in the area that has lost all living organisms that had existed there; it is called Secondary Succession. Newly created ponds, bare rock are examples of primary succession. Abandoned farmlands and burned forests are examples of secondary succession.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In hydrosere, the stages that come before and after the reed-swamp stage are, respectively,
options: submerged stage and submerged free-floating stage
submerged free-floating plant stage and marsh-meadow stage
submerged free-floating plant stage and scrub stage
questions.solution:
Ecological succession is a predictable process; therefore, it can be predicted which stage will come before or after any stage. The correct sequence of succession is:

Phytoplankton stage → submerged plant stage → submerged free floating plant stage → reed-swamp stage → marsh meadow stage → scrub stage → forest stage.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is corrcet regarding the ecosystem?
options: There is cyclic exchange of materials between living beings and environment.
The flow of energy is unidirectional.
questions.solution:
The ecosystem is defined as a system consists of a living community of plants, animals, and microbes together with their physical environment of air, water, soil, etc.

An ecosystem maintains a functional balance amongst its various components. This phenomenon is called homeostasis. The homeostasis or balance of nature is maintained through some control systems like carrying capacity of the ecosystem, the capacity of an ecosystem to recycle the wastes, feedback system, etc.

A functioning ecosystem exhibits biological and chemical activities, rates of plant production, the flow of energy, carbon storage, and nutrient cycling that are characteristic of most forests.

The energy flow in an ecosystem is said to be unidirectional because 90% of the energy gets used up by the organism in a trophic level and is released as heat, and only 10% of the energy is available to be transferred to next trophic level.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following will relate to vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels of ecosystem?
questions.solution: Biotic and abiotic components interact and form a physical structure which is unique for each type of ecosystem. Vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels is called stratification. For example, trees occupy top layer of a forest, smaller plants the second and weeds and grasses occupy the bottom layers. Pyramid of numbers provide information regarding the relationship between organisms at each trophic level in a ecosystem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following acts as ''natural scavengers''?
questions.solution: The detrivores together with the decomposers (bacteria, actinomycetes & fungi) are sometimes referred to as reducers. The two are also called scavengers because they clean the earth.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following accounts for 50% of the total cost of various ecosystem services?
options: Recreation and habitat for wild life
questions.solution: As per ecological economist Robert Constanza, soil formation accounts for about 50%, and contributions of other services like recreation and nutrient cycling are less than 10% each from the total cost of various ecosystem services. Climate regulation and habitat for wildlife each cost approximately 6%.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In how many trophic levels can humans function in a food chain?
questions.solution: Humans feed on vegetables and fruits. So they can be called primary consumers (Trophic level T2). Some humans also consume herbivores animals such as goat and lamb. So humans can be called secondary consumers (Trophic level T3). Humans also consume fishes such as salmon which are carnivorous animals. So humans can be tertiary consumers (Trophic level T4)

questions.q:
Which of the following is/are the structural character/s of an ecosystem?

Dominance, Species composition, Stratification, Nutrient cycle, Food Web complexity, Productivity
options: Nutrient cycle, Food Web complexity, Productivity
questions.solution: Dominance is the abundance of a species in an ecosystem, it affects the functioning of the ecosystem. Species composition is the identification and enumeration of different types of species present in the ecosystem. Vertical distribution of different species forming a canopy structure is called stratification. These are three important structural components of the ecosystem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and state how many of them are true?

(P) Primary succession, is a very slow process, taking thousands of years for the climax to be reached.

(Q) All succession whether taking place in water or land proceeds to a similar climax community, the mesic.

(R) As succession proceeds, the number and types of animals and decomposers also change.

(S) Saprophytes are not given any place in the ecological pyramids as they play no role in the ecosystem.
questions.solution: When one species occupy an area leading to declining or disappearance of other species; this changes in composition of species in any given area is called ecological succession. When succession occurs in an area where no living organism ever existed; it is called Primary Succession. There has to be soil for a biotic community to be established and it takes a hundred to thousand years for fertile soil to be produced hence, primary succession take is a slow process. Hydrarch succession taking place in water as well as xeric conditions taking place in dry areas, both proceed to mesic conditions that are neither too dry nor wet. Saprophytes though play a vital role, of degrading dead matter, in an ecosystem are not given any place in an ecological pyramid.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In a pond ecosystem, the shape of a pyramid of number is
questions.solution: The base of each pyramids represents the producers or the first trophic level while the apex represents tertiary or top level consumers. The pyramid of number for pond ecosystem is always upright. Phytoplanktons are chief producers, though their biomass is less but their number is maximum.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Consider the following statements concerning food chains.

I. Removal of 80% tigers from an area resulted in greatly increased growth of vegetation.
II. In a grassland ecosystem with deers being primary consumers, removal of most of the carnivores resulted in an increased population of deers.
III. The length of food chains is generally limited to 3 to 4 trophic levels due to energy loss.
IV. The length of food chains may vary from 2 to 8 trophic levels.

Which two of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution: The series of organisms eating one and being eaten by other is called food chain.  A simple food chain consists of producers, herbivores and carnivores.  The length of food chain is generally limited to 3-4 trophic levels due to energy loss.  In grazing food chain, the producers (i.e., plants) are eaten by herbivores (i.e., rabbit, dear, cow, etc) and are eaten by carnivores.  Therefore, the removal of most of the carnivores resulted in an increased population of deers.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following condition will inhibit decomposition?
questions.solution: Decomposition is largely an oxygen-requiring process. The rate of decomposition is controlled by chemical composition of detritus and climatic factors. In a particular climatic condition, decomposition rate is slower if detritus is rich in lignin and chitin, and quicker, if detritus is rich in nitrogen and water-soluble substances like sugars. Temperature and soil moisture are the most important climatic factors that regulate decomposition through their effects on the activities of soil microbes. Warm and moist environment favour decomposition whereas low temperature and anaerobiosis inhibit decomposition resulting in buildup of organic materials.

questions.solution: A local population adapted genetically to its particular environment is called ecotype. There may be several ecotypes of the same organism which show variation amongst them.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: How many trophic levels are there in a food chain?
questions.solution: Plants represent the first trophic level and the herbivores make the second trophic level. The primary carnivores constitute the third trophic level, and the secondary carnivores, such as large fish, man, etc. constitute the fourth trophic level of an ecosystem.

They are main contributors to ecosystem properties
questions.solution: The keystone species in an ecosystem are those who are the main contributors to the ecosystem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding food chain is false?
options: In an aquatic ecosystem, grazing food chain is the major conduit for energy flow.
In terrestrial ecosystems, a large fraction of energy flows through detritus food chain.
The detritus food chain begins with dead organic matter.
Primary consumers belong to the first trophic level.
questions.solution: All animals depend on plants directly or indirectly for their food needs. They are hence, called consumers and also heterotrophs. If they feed on the producer, the plants (belonging to the first trophic level), they are called primary consumers. Obviously the primary consumers will be herbivores. Some common herbivores are insects, birds and mammals in terrestrial ecosystem and molluscs in aquatic system. Thus, primary consumers belong to the second trophic level.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following ecosystem has the maximum amount of biomass production?
questions.solution: Biomass refers to the amount of living organic matter, Forest ecosystem has the maximum biomass, because it includes organisms of all trophic levels as compared to the pond, Lake or grassland ecosystem, In forest ecosystems productivity is also high that contributes to maximum biomass.

questions.solution: The amount of biomass or organic matter produced by plants by photosynthesis per unit area and over a period of time is called primary productivity. questions.subject: Botany

(ii) Energy flow

(iii) Decomposition

(iv) Stratification
questions.solution: The basic structural and functional unit of ecology is an ecosystem which is made up of abiotic and biotic components. There is a characteristic physical structure within each ecosystem due to the interaction of abiotic and biotic components. Species composition and stratification form the two main structural features of an ecosystem. For any ecosystem to function and sustain, solar energy supply is a basic requirement.

questions.solution: The great Barrier Reef - the largest system of coral reefs in the world - is more than 2,000 km in length and comprises 2,900 separate reefs and 940 islands. Its high species diversity includes more than 400 species of coral, 4,000 species of molluscs, 1,500 species of fish, 6 species of turtles, 35 species of seabirds and 23 species of sea mammals, The Great Barrier Reef is one of the richest and most complex natural systems in the world. questions.q: Which of these is not a correct difference between carbon cycle and phosphorus cycle?
options: Carbon cycle is a gaseous type of nutrient cycle while Phosphorus cycle is a sedimentary type of nutrient cycle.
The reservoir of carbon is ocean while the reservoir of phosphorus is rock
In carbon cycle, there is respiratory release of carbon into atmosphere while this doesn't happen in phosphorus cycle
Atmospheric inputs of phosphorus through rainfall are much larger than carbon inputs
questions.solution: The reservoir for gaseous type of nutrient cycle (e.g., nitrogen, carbon cycle) exists in the atmosphere and for the sedimentary cycle (e.g., sulphur and phosphorus cycle), the reservoir is located in Earth's crust. 71% of carbon is found dissolved in oceans. The natural reservoir of phosphorus is rock, which contains phosphorus in the form of phosphates. Unlike the carbon cycle, there is no respiratory release of phosphorus into the atmosphere. Atmospheric inputs of phosphorus through rainfall are much smaller than carbon input.

options: <math><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>–</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>–</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>–</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>

<math><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>–</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>–</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>–</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>

<math><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>–</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>–</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>–</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>
