questions.solution: Fragmentation, leaching, and catabolism are important steps of decomposition. Fragmentation is the process of breakdown of detritus, consisting of remains of dead plants and animals, into smaller particles by detrivores like an earthworm. The water-soluble inorganic nutrients obtained from the process of decomposition get precipitated as unavailable salts. This process is known as leaching. Degradation of detritus into simpler inorganic substances by bacterial and fungal enzymes is called catabolism.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A place, which used to be rocky and barren, has now turned into a lush green forest. The plant succession of the area is
questions.solution:
The rocky and barren place is deficient in water and lacks any organic matter, having only minerals in disintegrated or weathered state, the pioneer to colonies this primitive substration are crustose types of lichen.

Crustose lichens→ Foliose lichens → Moss→ Herbs → Shrub → tree.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Overlapping region between two ecosystems is called
questions.solution: The zone of transition between two different communities presenting a situation of overlapping is known as an ecotone.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In ecological succession
options: species response and community response will be observed.
species response and community response will not be observed.
only species response is observed without community response.
nether species response not community response is observed.
questions.solution: The primary succession means the development of communities only on a newly exposed habitat with no record of earlier vegetation. An important characteristic of all communities is that composition and structure constantly change in response to the changing environmental conditions. During ecological succession is a series of progressive changes in the species that make up a community is observed. This change is orderly and sequential, parallel with the changes in the physical environment. These changes lead finally to a community that is in near equilibrium with the environment.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is the correct representation of detritus food chain?
questions.solution: It begins with detritus such as dead bodies of animals or fallen leaves, which are then eaten by decomposers or detritivores. These detritivores are in turn consumed by their predators.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: ________________ leads to accumulation of a dark coloured amorphous substance called ________ that is highly resistant to microbial action and undergoes decomposition at an extremely slow rate.
questions.solution: Humification leads to accumulation of a dark coloured amorphous substance called humus that is highly resistant to microbial action and undergoes decomposition at an extremely slow rate. Being colloidal in nature it serves as a reservoir of nutrients. The humus is further degraded by some microbes and release of inorganic nutrients occur by the process known as mineralisation

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The total dry weight accessible to heterotrophs in an ecosystem will form the:
questions.solution: Gross primary productivity of an ecosystem is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis. A considerable amount of GPP is utilised by plants in respiration. Gross primary productivity minus respiration losses (R), is the net primary productivity (NPP). It is the available biomass for the consumption to heterotrophs (herbivores and decomposers)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Hydrarch succession and Xerarch succession doesn't differ in
questions.solution: Hydrach succession begins in water bodies and continues till mesic conditions are obtained. Xerach succession begins in dry land and continues till mesic conditions are obtained. Mesic condition in both successions is the same, neither too dry nor too wet. The community here is in near equilibrium with the environment and is called climax community. It is a forest.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The food chain in which microbes split energy rich compounds of the producer community is
questions.solution: Detritus food chain starts from dead organic matter acted upon by decomposers which in turn are eaten by detrivores consumers which are eaten by top consumers.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following pairs is a gaseous type of biogeochemical cycle?
questions.solution: Biogeochemical cycles are of two types: gaseous and sedimentary. In gaseous nutrient cycles, the materials involved in circulation between biotic and abiotic components of biosphere are gases or vapours and the reservoir pool is atmosphere or hydrosphere, e.g., carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, water. In sedimentary nutrient cycles, materials involved in circulation between biotic and abiotic components of biosphere are nongaseous and the reservoir pool is lithosphere, e.g., phosphorus, calcium, magnesium. Sulphur has both sedimentary and gaseous nutrient cycles.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Danny ate spinach, salad and mutton curry for lunch. At which of the following trophic levels did Danny function in this food chain?

(i) Producer

(ii) Primary Consumer

(iii) Secondary Consumer

(iv) Tertiary Consumer
questions.solution: Plants are the producers in the food chain. The organism consuming plants is the Primary consumer. The organism consuming animals which in turn derive energy from plants is a Secondary consumer. Thus in the above example Danny is consuming plants is a primary consumer as well as he had mutton which comes from goats which are dependent on plants for their food and acts as the secondary consumer also.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following best explains the abiotic components in a pond ecosystem?
options: Water with dissolved inorganic and organic substances
Water with dissolved inorganic and organic substances and also the soil at the bottom
questions.solution:
Pond is a shallow water body which is having all the four basic components of an ecosystem.

- Abiotic components : Water with dissolved inorganic and organic substances and the rich soil deposited at the bottom of the pond.

- Biotic components involve :

A. Autotrophs- Phytoplankton, some algae and the floating, submerged and marginal plants found at the edges.

B. Consumers- Zooplanktons, the free swimming and bottom dwelling forms.

C. Decomposers- Fungi, bacteria and flagellates (usually abundant at the sea floor).

- Pond is a self-sustainable unit.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following correctly represent the pyramid of biomass in aquatic ecosystem?
questions.solution: The total biomass of each trophic level can be represented by using a pyramid of biomass. In most ecosystems, the pyramid of biomass is an upright one. But in the aquatic ecosystem, the biomass pyramid is inverted. This is because the primary producers in the aquatic ecosystem are the phytoplanktons. These phytoplanktons are micro organisms and thus have very little biomass as compared to the aquatic animals who consume them and occupy the successive trophic levels in the food chain.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following groups is absolutely essential functional component of the ecosystem?
questions.solution: Ecosystem composed of biotic (living) and abiotic (non-living) component.  Biotic component includes producers, consumers and detritivores.  The producers and detritivores are absolutely essential functional component of the ecosystem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following suggests the main role of bacteria in the carbon cycle?
questions.solution: Bacteria are important decomposers in nature. Type play an important role in the recycling of nutrients by causing the breakdown of dead organic matter thus plays an important role in the carbon cycle. The most important bacteria involved in the carbon cycle is Pseudomonas denitrificans.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The correct sequence of plants in a hydrosere is
options: Oak → Lantana → Volvox → Hydrilla → Pistia → Scirpus
questions.solution:
The various stages in a hydrosere are well studied in ponds, pools or lakes. The various stages of hydrosere are :

(i) Phytoplankton stage, e.g., Some blue-green algae, green algae (Volvox), diatoms and bacteria, etc.

(ii)Rooted submerged stage, e.g., Hydrilla, Vallisneria, etc.

(iii) Floating stage, e.g., Nelumbo, Nymphaea, etc. Some free floating species are Pistia, Azolla, Lemna, etc.

(iv) Red-swamp stage, e.g., Species of Scirpus, Typha, etc.

(v) Sedge-meadow stage, e.g., Species of Cyperaeae and Gramineae.

(vi) Woodland stage, e.g., Lantana, Salix, Populus, etc.

(vii) Forest stage, e.g., Tropical rain forests, mixed forests of Almus, Acer, Quercus (oak), tropical deciduous forests.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The correct representation of the pyramid is,
options: Pyramid of energy in the grassland ecosystem
Pyramid of biomass in the grassland ecosystem
Pyramid of energy in the temperate ecosystem
Pyramid of energy in the tropical ecosystem
questions.solution: Upright pyramid: In the upright pyramid, the base occupied by producers is broad as compared to subsequent consumers, which gradually narrows down at the apex. It occurs in all the three kinds of pyramids. Pyramid of energy is always upright, can never be inverted, because when energy flows from a particular trophic level to the next trophic level, some energy is always lost as heat at each step. The given pyramid represents the grassland ecosystem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The trophic level of Cuscuta, Orobanche, and Albugo is
questions.solution: A parasitic plant is a plant that derives some or all of its nutritional requirement from another living plant. They make up about 1% of angiosperms and are in almost every biome in the world. All parasitic plants have modified roots, named haustoria (singular: haustorium), which penetrates the host plants, connecting them to the conductive system – either the xylem, the phloem, or both. This provides them with the ability to extract water and nutrients from the host. All these plants are parasitic.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: If we completely remove the decomposers from an ecosystem, the ecosystem functioning will be adversely affected because:
options: Herbivores will not receive solar energy
Rate of deposition of other component will be very high.
questions.solution: Heterotrophic organisms like bacteria and fungi act as decomposers which degrade the dead organic matter or detritus which in turn provides energy and nutrition. Decomposers secrete gastric enzymes resulting in the breakdown of dead organic matter into simple inorganic substances which are then absorbed in the soil and used by producers to grow. Hence if the decomposers are removed from the ecosystem, nutrients will not be available to producers which block the flow of minerals from producers to consumers.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which trophic level of a terrestrial ecosystem such as forest maximum energy can be found in organism?
questions.solution: T<sub>1</sub> or first tropic level in a terrestrial ecosystem is occupied by producer which traps solar energy and transfer it to successive tropic level. Maximum energy is always present in T<sub>1</sub> and energy flow is always unidirectional.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the option which is the exact representation of the picture given below.
questions.solution: Lichens are pioneer organisms on bare rocks as they corrode the rocks by secreting enzymes and convert it into soil. The crustose lichens are the first lichens to inhabit the rocks and are called as endothilic. It is a complex life form that is a symbiotic partnership of two separate organisms, a fungus, and algae. The dominant partner is the fungus, which gives the lichen the majority of its characteristics, from its thallus shape to its fruiting bodies.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the incorrect statement from the following.
options: Vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels is called stratification.
Secondary productivity is defined as the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers.
Leaching is the breakdown detritus into smaller particles.
Secondary productivity  <math><mo>=</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">G</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mo>–</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></math> .
questions.solution: Secondary productivity is the quantity of biomass produced at the level of consumer.  GPP is gross primary productivity, it is the total quantity of organic matter produced by producers.  <math><mi mathvariant="normal">G</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">P</mi><mo>–</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></math>  (respiratory loss) gives net primary productivity.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following is the characteristics of a biological community?
questions.solution: The characteristics of biological community are dominance, species diversity, trophic organisation, stratification, dynamism and stability. Organisms are not uniformly distributed throughout a community. They usually occur in definite zones. This spatial arrangement of populations is called stratification. Natality, mortality, age structure and sex ratio are the basic characteristics of a population.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
A Each trophic level, a certain mass of living material at a particular time called as__ P___.

B Breakdown of detritus into smaller particles, this process is called ____Q____.

Fill in the blanks with suitable word.
options:
P Q
Standing crop Fragmentation

P Q
Standing crop Stratification
questions.solution: Detritivores (e.g., earthworm) break down detritus into smaller particles. This process is called fragmentation. The total amount or number of living things or of one kind of living thing (such as an uncut farm crop, the fish in a pond, or organisms in an ecosystem) in a particular area at any given time is called standing crop.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Identify the correct sequence of involvement, according to ecological succession.
questions.solution: The gradual and fairly predictable change in the species composition of a given area is called ecological succession. During succession some species colonise an area and whereas populations of other species decline and even disappear. The entire sequence of communities that successively change in a given area are called sere(s). The individual transitional communities are termed seral stages or seral communities. Ultimately a stable climax forest community is formed. The climax community remains stable as long as the environment remains unchanged.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Robert Constanza and his colleagues have put a price tag of US $ 33 trillion a year on
questions.solution: Robert Constanza and his colleagues have very recently tried to put price tags on nature’s life-support services. Researchers have put an average price tag of US 33 trillion a year on these fundamental ecosystems services, which is largely taken for granted because they are free. This is nearly twice the value of the global gross national product GNP which is (US 18 trillion).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The graph below shows the changes in two populations of herbivores in a grassy field. A possible reason for these changes is that
options: population B competed more successfully for food than population A did.
all of the plant populations in this habitat decreased.
population A consumed the members of population B.
population A produced more offspring than population B did.
questions.solution: If population B increased while population A decreased, these organisms were probably in competition for the same food (grass) and population B was better adapted. Hence population A is competitively being excluded from the population.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which is CORRECT order of seral stages in hydrach?
options: Phytoplankton-Rooted submerged stage-Rooted free floating plant-reed swamp stage-marsh meadow stage-scrub stage-forest
Scrub stages-forest-reed swamp stage-marsh meadow stage-submerged free floating plant stage-submerged plant-phytoplankton
Submerged plant-marsh meadow stage-scrub stages-forest-phytoplankton-submerged free floating plant stage-reed swamp stage
Phytoplankton-red swamp stage-scrub stages-forest-submerged plant-submerged free floating plant stage-marsh meadow stage
questions.solution: Ecological succession is defined as the process of gradual and predictable change in the species composition of an area. Primary succession occurs in those areas where no organism ever existed whereas secondary succession takes place in those areas where organisms once existed but now have lost them due to some reason. In Primary succession of wet land into forest the first to appear are the phytoplanktons. They are replaced by submerged plants and later submerged and floating plants both appear. Gradually it passes through the reed swamp and marsh meadow stages and lastly scrubs appear before forming it into a forest land.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The sudden mass killing of fishes is likely to be seen in a
questions.solution: Organic pollutants provide nutrients for stimulating the growth of algae and other plants. Algal bloom reduces the availability of light to submerged plants consumes more oxygen in decomposition. This reduces the availability of oxygen to other life forms leading to death of organisms. This is known as eutrophication.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The amount of nutrients such as carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, calcium etc. present in the soil at any given time is referred to as
questions.solution: A definite amount of living material present at each trophic level at a specific time is called a standing crop. It can be measured as biomass or a number in a unit area. The nutrients which are necessary for growth such as carbon, phosphorous, calcium, etc. are present in abiotic components such as soil and are known as standing state. Mineralisation is the process by which inorganic nutrients are released into the soil by the degradation of humus by microbes. Hence, the answer is standing state.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: If 20kJ energy is available at the producer level, then how much energy will be transferred to the lion in the food chain: Producer <math><mo>→</mo></math> deer <math><mo>→</mo></math> lion?
questions.solution: As per the Ten percent energy transfer law introduced by Lindeman-'During the transfer of energy from organic food from one trophic level to the next, only about ten percent of the energy from organic matter is stored as flesh.' In a typical food chain, only ten percent of the energy is passed to the next consumer in the unidirectional manner. Since, producer has 20kJ, the deer will have 2kJ. Hence, the lion will only get 0.2kJ

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
How many of the following statements are incorrect?

(i) Decomposition is largely an anaerobic process.

(ii) Fragmentation, leaching, and catabolism occur simultaneously on detritus.

(iii) The vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels is called stratification.

(iv) The pond is a deep water body.

(v) The rate of decomposition is controlled by the chemical composition of detritus and climatic factors.
questions.solution: Decomposition is largely an aerobic process, and requires oxygen. A pond is a shallow water body in which all the four basic components of an ecosystem are well exhibited.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A more accurate measure of biomass will be in terms of
questions.solution: The standing crop is measured as the mass of living organism or biomass. The biomass of a species is expressed in terms of fresh weight or dry weight. Measurement of biomass in terms of dry weight is more accurate as fresh weight shows more seasonal variation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The rate of decomposition of detritus is accelerated
options: If the detritus contains lignin chitin, tannins and cellulose.
If the detritus is present in acidic soil
If the moisture and aeration are at optimum
questions.solution: Detritus is the dead organic material which includes the parts or bodies of dead organisms and their faecal matter. These organic content are broken down to inorganic substances by the process called decomposition. It is brought about by decomposers. Decomposition is a mainly an oxygen dependent process and its rate is dependent on chemical composition and climatic factors. Temperature and moisture play an important role in rate of decomposition. Enough supply of oxygen and proper moisture accelerates the decomposition process.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The amount of biomass or organic matter produced per unit area over a time period by the plants during photosynthesis is called
questions.solution:
Each trophic level has a certain mass of living material at a particular time called as the standing crop. The standing crop is measured as the mass of living organism (biomass) or the number in a unit area. The biomass of a species is expressed in terms of fresh weight or dry weight. Measurement of biomass in terms of dry weight is more accurate.
 Primary production is defined as the amount of biomass or organic matter produced per unit area over a time period by plants during photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following shows a pyramid of biomass in a pond ecosystem?
questions.solution: In aquatic ecosystem, the pyramid of biomass may be inverted. For example, biomass of zooplanktons is higher than that of phytoplanktons as life span of former is longer and the latter multiply much faster though having shorter life span. A number of generations of phytoplanktons may thus be consumed by single generation of zooplanktons. Biomass of fish may still be larger as fishes are larger in size with longer life span and a number of generations of zooplanktons can be consumed by fishes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The energy available to the organism at the third trophic level is called
questions.solution:
Carnivores are organisms which obtain nutrient by killing and eating other animals. These form the secondary consumers present in the third trophic level and are preceded by the herbivore in the food chain. The rate of assimilation of food energy by consumers is called secondary productivity and this energy is available to carnivores as they are the consumers.

Total production of organic matter is called gross primary productivity and the energy left after utilization of producers is termed net primary productivity. Community productivity is the difference between GPP and the community respiration.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is expected to have the highest value (gm/m<sup>2</sup>/yr) in a grassland ecosystem?
questions.solution: Grasslands will have highest value of gross production. Net production is obtained after subtracting the respiratory utilization from grass production. Secondary and tertiary production is related with secondary and tertiary consumers respectively.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Productivity is the rate of production of biomass expressed in terms of

(i) kcal/m3/yr
(ii) g/m2/yr
(iii) g/yr
(iv) kcal/m2/yr
questions.solution: The rate of synthesis of energy containing organic matter or biomass by any trophic level per unit area in unit time is described as its productivity. It is measured as weight (e.g., g/m2/yr) or energy (e.g., Kcal/m2/yr).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The pyramid of energy in a forest ecosystem is
questions.solution: Pyramid of energy is always upright in all types of ecosystem as energy goes on decreasing with each and every trophic level.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: All these statements about trophic levels and ecosystems are false except
options: Trophic level represents a functional level, not a species as such
A given species never occupies more than one trophic level in the same ecosystem at the same  time
In most ecosystems, producers are less in number and biomass than the herbivores
Pyramid of energy can never be upright.
questions.solution: Organisms occupy a specific position in an ecosystem based on their source of food which is known as trophic levels. In trophic levels, the first level is occupied by producers second by herbivores and third level by carnivores. These levels do not depict the species but their functional level. A sparrow becomes a primary consumer when it eats seeds and secondary consumers when it feeds on worms. Hence a given specie can occupy more than one trophic level at the same time in the ecosystem. In the most ecosystem, the pyramid of energy and biomass is upright as producers more in number and biomass than herbivores and herbivores are more in number and biomass than carnivores.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and select the correct statements.

(i) DFC begins with dead inorganic matter.
(ii) DFC is the major conduit for energy flow in a terrestrial ecosystem
(ii) GFC of aquatic ecosystem is longer than a terrestrial ecosystem.
(iv) DFC and GFC are completely separate chains.
questions.solution: DFC is longer than GFC in terrestrial ecosystem while GFC is longer than DFC in aquatic ecosystem. Detritus is more in terrestrial ecosystem and less in aquatic ecosystem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
During an ecological succession, many changes occur. Select the wrong statement with respect to succession.

(i) Some species colonise and some species disappear

(ii) Diversity will not change during succession.

(iii) The total biomass increases.

(iv) The species number increases.
questions.solution: The gradual and fairly predictable change in the species composition of a given area is called ecological succession. During succession diversity biomass increases and stability also increases.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Of the total incident solar radiation, the proportion of PAR is
questions.solution: Of the total incident solar radiation only less than 50% is photosynthetically active radiation and only 2 - 10 % of which is used up by plants in photosynthesis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Rate of biomass production is expressed as:
options: <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi></mrow></mfenced><mi> </mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>

<math><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">g </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>
questions.solution: The amount of biomass produced per unit area over a period of time is called primary productivity expressed in weight  <math><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>–</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></math>  or energy  <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced></math> . The rate at which this biomass is produced is called productivity. To compare the productivity of different ecosystems it is expressed by units  <math><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo>–</mo><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mo>–</mo><mn>1</mn></math>  or  <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo>–</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfenced><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">y</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mo>–</mo><mn>1</mn></math> . It is divided into gross primary productivity and net primary productivity. The rate at which organic matter is produced during photosynthesis is gross primary productivity and the remaining biomass after the respiratory loss is net primary productivity.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The order of organism in an aquatic food chain is
options: Crustacea, Seal, Fish, Polar Bear, Diatom
questions.solution: Diatoms are producer, crustacea is primary consumer, fish is secondary consumer, seal is top consumer and bacteria are decomposers.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following constitutes of a micro-ecosystem?
questions.solution:
A community of organisms interacting with abiotic component in a particular region/area will be called as ecosystem. The living and non-living components are linked together by the nutrient cycles and energy flow through each trophic level.

Regions or locations defined by critical environmental factors within small spaces contain the micro-ecosystem. Pond is a classic example of microecosystem with limited water volume generally for short duration. These are generally colonized by organisms which are do not live in water continuously and by organisms possessing drought-resistant spores in their life cycle.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In aquatic ecosystem, __(i)__ is the major conduit for energy flow, as against in the terrestrial ecosystem, a much larger fraction of energy flows through the __(ii)___ than ___(iii)_ .
questions.solution:
GFC- grazing food chain and DFC- detritus food chain.

Food chain starting with dead organic matter is DFC where was food chain starting with a producer is GFC. DFC begins with decomposers and in aquatic system, decomposition is very low. Thus, GFC forms the main channel of energy flow in it. Where in land ecosystem, decomposition rate is higher as a result more amount of energy flows through DFC than GFC.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The amount of living biomass present in a unit area of an ecosystem at a given time is referred to as:
questions.solution:
Standing crop is the total amount of living material in a specified population at a particular time, generally expressed as biomass. The standing crop may show variation at different times of the year.

Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is the rate at which plants incorporate atmospheric carbon through photosynthesis. (Definition)

Gross primary production (GPP) is the rate at which an ecosystem's producers capture and store a given amount of chemical energy as biomass in a given length of time. (Definition)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: ________ are important decomposers that cause decay and decomposition of dead bodies of plants and animals.
questions.solution: The organic content of the dead and decaying organisms is broken down to inorganic substances by the process called decomposition. It is brought about by decomposers. questions.solution:

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Based on the source of their nutrition or food, organism occupies a specific place in the food chain which is known as their:

Producer belongs to first trophic level, herbivores to second and carnivores to third trophic level.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Secondary productivity is defined as
options: the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis.
the available biomass for the consumption to heterotrophs.
the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers.
gross primary productivity minus respiration losses.
questions.solution:
Gross primary productivity of an ecosystem is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis. A considerable amount of GPP is utilised by plants in respiration.

Gross primary productivity minus respiration losses (R), is the net primary productivity (NPP).

GPP – R = NPP

Net primary productivity is the available biomass for the consumption to heterotrophs (herbiviores and decomposers).

Secondary productivity is defined as the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers.

questions.subject: Botany

The dead and decaying organic content are broken down to inorganic substances by the process called decomposition. It is brought about by decomposers. Producers and decomposers help in maintaining the food chain.

Removal of tigers from an area will result in decreased growth of vegetation of that area as the increased population of deer will consume more vegetation. Sparrow in a food chain can exist at two different trophic levels, while feeding on grains it occupies second trophic level, while feeding on worms they occupy third trophic level.

(ii) Pyramid of numbers is inverted in grassland and upright in aquatic ecosystem.
(iii) Pyramid of energy depicts the rate of energy flow or productivity at successive trophic levels.

options:

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Decomposition is inhibited during:
questions.solution: Decomposition is largely an oxygen-requiring process. The rate of decomposition is controlled by chemical composition of detritus and climatic factors. In a particular climatic condition, decomposition rate is slower if detritus is rich in lignin and chitin, and quicker, if detritus is rich in nitrogen and water soluble substances like sugars. Temperature and soil moisture are the most important climatic factors that regulate decomposition through their effects on the activities of soil microbes. Warm and moist environment favour decomposition whereas low temperature and anaerobiosis inhibit decomposition resulting in build up of organic materials.

both organic and inorganic nutrients from detritus

Humus is colloidal in nature which serves as a reservoir of inorganic nutrients. So, during mineralization inorganic nutrients are withdrawn with the help of microbes. At the level of detritus, fragmentation takes place due to which smaller particles are formed and during catabolism, detritus degrades into smaller inorganic substances with the help of bacterial and fungal enzymes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following processes of decomposition produces a substance resistant to microbial action?
questions.solution: Detritivores (e.g., earthworm) break down detritus into smaller particles. This process is called fragmentation. By the process of leaching, watersoluble inorganic nutrients go down into the soil horizon and get precipitated as unavailable salts. Bacterial and fungal enzymes degrade detritus into simpler inorganic substances. This process is called as catabolism. It is important to note that all the above steps in decomposition operate simultaneously on the detritus.Humification and mineralisation occur during decomposition in the soil. Humification leads to accumulation of a dark coloured amorphous substance called humus that is highly resistant to microbial action and undergoes decomposition at an extremely slow rate. Being colloidal in nature it serves as a reservoir of nutrients. The humus is further degraded by some microbes and release of inorganic nutrients occur by the process known as mineralisation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is considered a man-made ecosystem?
questions.solution:
TYPES OF ECOSYSTEM:
Ecosystem varies greatly in size from a small pond to a large forest or a sea. Many ecologies regard the entire biosphere as a global ecosystem as a composite of all local ecosystem on earth. Since this system is too much big and complex to be studied at one time, so to make the study easier, it is broadly divided into two basic categories.
i) Terrestrial Ecosystem: It occurs over land e.g., forest, grassland, desert.
ii) Aquatic Ecosystem: It occurs in water bodies e.g., pond, lake, river (freshwater), wetland, sea, estuaries (salt water).
Similarly, w.r.t. human interference the ecosystems are of two types:
i) Natural ecosystem: It develops in nature without human support or interference e.g., forests, marine ecosystem.
ii) Anthropogenic ecosystem or man-made ecosystem: It is the one which is created and maintained by human beings e.g., crop fields, garden, aquarium, Agro ecosystem or agriculture is the largest manmade ecosystem.

questions.solution:
The rate of biomass production is called productivity. It is expressed in terms of g–2 yr–1 or (kcal m–2)yr–1 to compare the productivity of different ecosystems. It can be divided into gross primary productivity (GPP) and net primary productivity (NPP). 
Net primary productivity is the available biomass for the consumption to heterotrophs (herbiviores and decomposers).
Primary productivity depends on the plant species inhabiting a particular area. It also depends on a variety of environmental factors, availability of nutrients and photosynthetic capacity of plants. Therefore, it varies in different types of ecosystems. The annual net primary productivity of the whole biosphere is approximately 170 billion tons (dry weight) of organic matter. Of this, despite occupying about 70 per cent of the surface, the productivity of the oceans are only 55 billion tons.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following can accelerate the rate of decomposition of the detritus?
options: If the detritus contains lignin, chitin, tannins and cellulose
If the detritus is present in acidic soil
If the moisture and aeration are at optimum
If the temperature is below <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>
questions.solution:
Factors Affecting Decomposition: The rate of decomposition of detritus is controlled by the chemical nature of detritus and a number of climatic factors given below.
a) Chemical nature of detritus. Decomposition of detritus is slow if it contains lignin, chitin, tannins (phenolics) and cellulose. It is rapid if detritus possesses more of nitrogenous compounds (like proteins, nucleic acids) and water-soluble reserve carbohydrates or sugars.
b)Temperature and c) soil moisture is the most important climatic factors that regulate decomposition through their effects on the activities of soil microbes.
d) Aeration: It is required for the activity of decomposers and detritivores. Reduced aeration will slow down the process of decomposition.

e) Salinity: The alkaline soil increase the detritus breakdown.
So, the warm and moist environment favour decomposition whereas low temperature and anaerobiosis inhibit decomposition resulting in buildup of organic materials.
